entries.bestHook: Two people born on the same day can share a star sign and have almost nothing else in common on the chart. Editorial pick (no performance data): challenges a specific belief the reader holds and opens a concrete curiosity gap.
entries.weakestHook: A quiet promise. Editorial pick: abstract opener with no curiosity or concrete stakes; the privacy message is strong but the first line does not stop a scroll.
entries.oneChange: On Facebook, replace the generic link-in-bio CTA with the actual free-chart URL plus a UTM tag in the post text. Reason: Facebook supports clickable in-post links and Facebook post link clicks are the one per-post click-to-chart signal Metricool exposes; with the link only in bio, next week's review still cannot tell which hook drives chart draws. Instagram stays link-in-bio (it cannot carry post links).

entries.cta: Free chart URL tideglyph.com/chart in every caption (clean, no UTM).

entries.clicksToFreeChart: Still no measurable signal. entries.bestHook: 'Two people born weeks apart can share a star sign and still have almost nothing else in common on the chart.' Editorial pick backed by the thin reach signal: the sharpest statement of the whole-chart differentiator and the furthest-traveled post of the week.
entries.weakestHook: 'As the Sun finishes its trip through Libra.' Reached 0 on Instagram and 1 on Facebook, the week's lowest. It leans on the generic sun-sign framing the brand positions against, so the opener works against the differentiator.
entries.oneChange: Make Monday's daily 'today's sky' post a short Reel (vertical video) instead of a static image. Reason: reach is the binding constraint. Static feed photos on an 8-day-old account are shown almost only to existing followers (near zero), while Reels are the one organic surface Instagram distributes to non-followers. Until posts reach people, no hook or CTA test can produce signal.
entries.note: Prior oneChange (FB-only clickable UTM link) is still pending Daniel's decision on splitting FB/IG into separate posts. It was partially realised in that today's-sky captions now include the raw chart URL, but photo-post link clicks still read 0. Not repeated as this week's change because distribution, not measurement, is now the bottleneck.

entries.ranking: (saves+shares)/reach = 0 for every post again: no saves or shares on either network, so the target metric still cannot rank posts. Ranked on raw reach as the distribution proxy (method B1: while reach is the binding constraint, read distribution, not hooks or CTAs). Furthest-traveled: the Instagram Moon-in-Cancer Reel, reach 9 / 11 views, the first Reel and the only item to break past single-digit static reach (static feed posts ran 1-5).
entries.clicksToFreeChart: No measurable signal. Facebook post link clicks = 0 across all posts (reach too low for clicks regardless); the Oct 29 FB Reel carried the UTM chart link in-caption and recorded 0 link clicks on reach 0. Instagram stays link-in-bio, no per-post click data.
entries.bestHook: Oct 29 Moon-in-Cancer Reel: 'What makes a place feel like home to you?' Furthest-traveled item of the week. In plain terms it names a feeling everyone recognises and invites a one-word answer, and it rode the Reel format that actually reaches non-followers. Runner-up on structure: the pillar 'Ever read your horoscope and felt it was written for a stranger?', which opens on the reader's own experience (problem first) before any astrology. Both are editorial reads: reach is still too thin to crown a hook.
entries.weakestHook: The today's-sky posts that open on planetary mechanics before any human angle, e.g. Oct 25 'With Venus moving backward through the sky, today's meeting with the Sun has a reflective, looking-back quality.' A cold reader has no reason to care by line one; the relatable question is buried under the jargon. Lowest views-per-reach of the week. Caveat: single-digit reach makes this a read, not a verdict.
entries.oneChange: Format, for Monday 2026-11-02: make the 18:00 pillar slot a Reel/video too, so both Monday slots are video rather than one Reel plus one static image. The week's single Reel reached 9 vs 1-5 for every static feed post, and on a roughly 5-follower account Reels are the one format Instagram shows to non-followers. Reach is the binding constraint in launch (method B1), so move the static pillars toward video before testing hooks or CTAs.
entries.crossBrandLesson: First hard number behind the already-recorded launch-weeks rule (B1): on a near-empty account a single Reel reached 9 people vs 1-5 for static feed posts. Genuinely cross-brand but n=1 so far; proposed as the first B2 'Content that works' data point once a second week confirms it. No method change needed this week.
